slides.title: Entering the Third Dimension
slides.visual_hint: A flat 2D blueprint rising into a 3D glass box.
slides.narration: Area covers a flat floor, but volume fills an entire room. We measure volume using unit cubes.

slides.title: The Floor Layer
slides.visual_hint: A grid of 4 cubes long by 3 cubes wide.
slides.narration: Look at the base. A length of four and a width of three creates a floor of twelve cubes.

slides.title: Stacking the Height
slides.visual_hint: Five layers of twelve cubes stacking vertically.
slides.narration: Now stack that base five layers high. Each layer holds twelve cubes.

slides.title: The Volume Equation
slides.narration: Multiply length times width times height. Four times three times five equals sixty cubic units.

slides.title: No Gaps, No Overlaps
slides.visual_hint: The box sealing tight with solid blue glowing cubes.
slides.narration: Every single cube fits perfectly inside with no gaps and no overlaps.

slides.title: Master of Dimensions
slides.narration: You now understand volume from the foundation to the ceiling. Great questing!
